children.translated_text:
Verse 87, number 15: <s>Ledarī</s> in the history of King <s>Lava</s> himself.
	Here, the etymology:
	According to the statement of the one-syllable lexicon composed by <s>Śiva</s>: '<s>la</s>' is known [to mean] 'remainder' and 'fear' — thus '<s>lo</s>' means fear; '<s>le</s>' means 'in fear,' that is, at the time of the arising of fear; and '<s>darī</s>' means 'cave.'
	That which appears deep, impenetrable, and difficult to cross — that is <s>Ledarī</s>.
	Alternatively, according to the one-syllable lexicon: '<s>da</s>' is declared by the learned to [mean] 'wife,' 'giving,' 'cutting,' and 'giver.'
	'<s>Le</s>' means 'in fear'; '<s>da</s>' [means] 'cutting'; 'fear-cutting' — she who gives (<s>rāti</s>) that, who flows — [that is <s>Ledarī</s>].
	The meaning is: when fear arises, she who cuts it off, the destroyer of fear.
	Such is this river.
	Some, relying on the <s>Bhṛṅgīśa Saṃhitā</s>, also call this <s>Ledarī</s> river by the name '<s>Lambodarī</s>.'
	Therein, '<s>lambam</s>' [means] 'water'; of the '<s>raya</s>' (current) — he is '<s>Lambodara</s>' (pot-bellied), that is, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>; the river that issued from his mouth — its designation is by the word '<s>Lambodarī</s>.'
	On the route of the <s>Cāmareśvara</s> (Amarnath) pilgrimage, at the place called <s>Gaṇeśabal</s>, there stands in the middle of the river a greatly venerated and famous stone image of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
	From the trunk of that image, which bears the very form of an elephant, this river appears to emerge as if released from a drinking vessel.
	However, the name <s>Ledarī</s> for this river also has an etymologically sound and textually consistent [explanation].
	For in this cluster of towns called <s>Dakṣiṇapārśva</s> (the Southern Side), in which this river flows, there is a village named <s>Lidar</s> situated on the bank of this river; therefore, this river has also become famous by that name.
	Because the river that flows through the village <s>Lidar</s> — she is the <s>Ledarī</s> river.
	In the <s>Bhṛṅgīśa Saṃhitā</s>, in the description of the greatness of <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>, this river is mentioned by this very name.
	Thus: 'As long as the <s>Cākā</s> flows, as long as the <s>Ledarī</s> river is full of water, as long as the twin <s>Nāgas</s> called <s>Kamalas</s> remain in the form of fish, as long as the radiant sun shines in the sky eternally by the power of time — so long does one who performs <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) at the <s>Sūryakṣetra</s> (Field of the Sun) dwell in heaven forever.'
	Such passages indeed illuminate the name <s>Ledarī</s>. Between the two regions on the southern side of this very river, the river flows in the middle.
	The villagers, in modern times, call this <s>Lambodarī</s> or <s>Ledarī</s> river by the name '<s>Lidar Ār</s>.'
	Therein, that river which, being filled with large boulders in the middle and flowing with extreme velocity, is difficult to cross —
	its name in the Kashmiri language is '<s>Ār</s>.'
	And this village named <s>Lidar</s>, which has become the seat of this river — its name in the village language is indeed '<s>Lidar</s>.'
	This village called <s>Lidar</s> is situated within the well-known <s>Dacchunpor Pargaṇa</s> (Southern township), on the bank of the <s>Ledarī</s> river.
	The name of this <s>Lambodarī</s> too, according to villagers, is simply '<s>Lidar</s>' — because this river originates from the place called <s>Gaṇeśabal</s>.
	Its name in the Kashmiri language is well-known as '<s>Gaṇiśabal</s>.'
	Therein, '<s>Gaṇiśa</s>' means <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and '<s>bal</s>' means 'place' — that is the meaning.
	This place called <s>Gaṇeśabal</s> is the first halting-station on the <s>Amareśvara</s> (Amarnath) pilgrimage.
	From this, at a distance of three <s>krośas</s> (about 6 miles), having traversed the road, [one reaches] the place called <s>Pahalgām</s>, which is the second halting-station of the <s>Amareśvara</s> pilgrimage.
	This village named <s>Lidar</s> is at a distance of twelve <s>krośas</s> to the west from <s>Anantanāga</s>.
	Here there is a temple (<s>mandira</s>) — a house of the gods — mostly ruined, constructed of large stones.
	That site was built by King <s>Meghavāhana</s>, described in the third <s>taraṅga</s> (chapter), in the ninetieth year of the <s>Vikramāditya</s> [era] — and so forth.
	Obtained from the <s>Mandirasaṃgraha</s> (Collection of Temples) and placed here.
16. <s>Levāra</s>

children.text:
ślokasaṃ 87 nambara 16 lavasya caritre levāraṃ |
	yasya levārasya niruktiḥ |
	laḥ śeṣe ca bhaye khyāta iti |
	tathā vaḥ sāntvane rasevāte ity ekākṣarakośokteś ca levighnāde bhaye vaṃ sāntvanaṃ tatnivāraṇarūpamāsam antāt rāti dadāti yaḥ sa levāraḥ |
	vighnanivārako gaṇeśaḥ |
	tathā ca nīlamatavarṇyaṃ mānadevāyatanakīrtanākhye prastāve
children.translated_text:
Verse 87, number 16: <s>Levāra</s> in the account of <s>Lava</s>.
	The etymology of this <s>Levāra</s>:
	'<s>la</s>' is known [to mean] 'remainder' and 'fear' — thus.
	And '<s>va</s>' [means] 'consolation' and 'enjoyment,' according to the single-syllable lexicon; from '<s>le</s>' [meaning] 'obstacle' and 'fear,' '<s>va</s>' [meaning] 'consolation,' that is, the removal of obstacles — he who gives (<s>rāti</s>) that at the end is <s>Levāra</s>.
	[That is,] <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, the remover of obstacles.
	And as described in the <s>Nīlamata</s> [Purāṇa], in the passage called the 'Enumeration of the Temples of <s>Mānadeva</s>':
<s>Bhūrjasvāmī</s>, <s>Hiḍambeśa</s>, <s>Levāra</s>, the glorious <s>Vināyaka</s>,
<s>Utaṅkeśa</s>, <s>Guhāvāsī</s>, <s>Bhīmeśa</s>, and <s>Saumukha</s> likewise,
<s>Bhadreśvara</s> and <s>Mahāsya</s>, and the two [called] <s>Mahāśana</s> and <s>Gaveṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Paulastya</s> and <s>Girivāsī</s>, and <s>Jayeśvara</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: ekaikam ebhyo dṛṣṭvā tu gaṇeśaṃ susamāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: By seeing each one of these <s>Gaṇeśa</s> [images] with concentrated mind,
one attains the accomplishment of [one's] purpose and enjoys meritorious fruit.

children.text:
ity ādau |
	asya levārākhyagaṇeśasya kaśmīrasthagaṇeśamūrtiṣu varṇyamānatvaṃ sphuṭatayā bhavati |
	eṣā gaṇeśamūrtiḥ pūrvoktaledarīnadyā vāmapārśve yo 'dhunā grāmīṇabhāṣāvyavahṛtau khourporpargaṇa iti nāma dhārayati tasminn eva pradeśe sarvaviditā vartate |
	asya gaṇeśasya nāmnevāyaṃ gaṇeśamūrtyāśrayavān grāmo levar iti nāmnaiva prakhyāta[...]ḥ sampannaḥ vartate |
	cāyaṃ grāmo 'smin puragaṇe levarśabdābhidheyo grāmīṇaiḥ kathyamānaḥ |
	asya grāmasya nikaṭe 'nyo 'pi grāmaḥ sarvaviditaḥ sīr ityākhyo bhavati |
	tasyaivaṃ kiṃcid dūratāyām ayaṃ grāmaḥ pūrvam eva levārākhyasya gaṇapater āśrayatayaiva tādṛśanāmayuta eva tena varṇyamānena lavarājñā agrahāratvavyapadeśavān samapādi |
	ata eva paṇḍitakalhaṇenāpi prathame taraṅge
children.translated_text:
— thus and so forth. That this <s>Gaṇeśa</s> named <s>Levāra</s> is described among the <s>Gaṇeśa</s> images situated in <s>Kaśmīra</s> is clearly manifest.
	This <s>Gaṇeśa</s> image is well-known in the very region on the left bank of the aforementioned <s>Ledarī</s> river, which now bears the name <s>Khourporpargaṇa</s> in the vernacular language.
	The village that houses this <s>Gaṇeśa</s> image is famous by the very name <s>Levar</s>, after the name of this <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
	And this village is called by the villagers with the word <s>Levar</s> in this district.
	Near this village there is also another well-known village called <s>Sīr</s>.
	At some distance from that, this village, having borne the name of <s>Levāra</s>-named <s>Gaṇapati</s> as its patron deity since ancient times, was designated as an <s>agrahāra</s> (Brahmin land-grant) by the king <s>Lava</s> described [in the Rājataraṅgiṇī].
	Therefore, even by <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s>, in the first <s>taraṅga</s> (chapter):
Having given the <s>agrahāra</s> (land-grant) of <s>Levāra</s> at the <s>Ledarī</s> [river] to the assembly of Brahmins,
he, the mighty-armed one whose glory and valor were unrivaled in heaven, ascended [to the celestial realm].

children.text:
ity ādyuktam |
	anayaiva vidhayā yo 'yaṃ grāmo levārākhyaḥ pūrvam eva babhūva |
	sa eva rājñāpi brāhmaṇebhyo 'grahārasamarpaṇakāle ca pūrvaprakhyātanāmnaiva saṃsthāpitaḥ |
	dānavelāyām api gaṇeśamūrtyāśrayatvavyapadiṣṭaṃ levārākhyaṃ nāmaiva rājñāpy asyāpi tamasyeti budhyate |
	kathayanti ca tatratyāḥ |
	asmin grāme eko mahāvṛkṣo yaṃ vṛkṣaṃ kāśmīrikā braṇ iti śabdenākārayanti |
	tenāpy upalakṣaṇībhūto bhavati sa eva vṛkṣo 'py asyoktagaṇeśasyādhiṣṭhānībhūto bhavati |
	yato bahavo vṛkṣāḥ anena braṇvṛkṣena kathyamānāḥ kaśmīradeśe devatāmūrtīnām adhiṣṭhānībhūtāḥ sarvato darīdṛśyante iti śam ||
children.translated_text:
— thus it was stated above.
	In this very manner, this village named <s>Levāra</s> had already existed since ancient times.
	It was established by the king himself with its previously well-known name even at the time of offering the <s>agrahāra</s> to the Brahmins.
	It is understood that even at the time of the gift, the name <s>Levāra</s>, designated by its being the abode of the <s>Gaṇeśa</s> image, was [recognized as such] by the king as well.
	And the local people relate:
	In this village there is one great tree, which the Kashmiris call by the word '<s>braṇ</s>.'
	This tree serves as a distinguishing mark, and this very tree also serves as the abode of the aforementioned <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
	For many trees called by this name '<s>braṇ</s>-tree' are seen everywhere in the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s> as abodes of divine images. Thus all is well.
17. <s>Kuruhāra</s>

children.text:
ślokasaṃ 88 nambara 17 kuśasya rājṇo varṇane kuruhār |
	asya nirvacanam |
	kaś cātmāpi samākhyātaḥ kaḥ pradeśa udāhṛta iti kośamatena |
	kair nānāvidhajalasthalādipradeśaiḥ urur mahān ata eva hāro manoharaś ca yaḥ sa kuruhāraḥ |
	nānāvidhapradeśamattayāntyā ledarīnadyā hāro muktāhāra iva yaḥ so 'pi kuruhāraḥ |
	atha vā kurunāmakair janapadair etaddeśanivāsibhir hriyate yo 'grahāratayāgra eva so 'pi kuruhāraḥ |
	pūrvam etan nāmni pradeśe kuru ityākhyāṃ bibhrāṇā vāstavyā babhūvuḥ |
	tair yato 'sya grāmasya sasyādisampattir ādāv eva hriyate smāto 'pi kuruhāraḥ |
	ata eva paṇḍitakalhaṇenāpi
children.translated_text:
Verse 88, number 17: <s>Kuruhāra</s> in the description of King <s>Kuśa</s>.
	Its etymology:
	'<s>Ka</s>' is also called the self (<s>ātman</s>), and '<s>ka</s>' denotes a region, according to the lexicon.
	That which is vast (<s>uru</s>) by means of diverse regions of water, land, and so forth, and hence is a garland (<s>hāra</s>), that is, enchanting — that is <s>Kuruhāra</s>.
	Alternatively, that which is like a necklace of pearls, a garland [formed] by the <s>Ledarī</s> river running through diverse regions — that too is <s>Kuruhāra</s>.
	Or, that which is taken (<s>hriyate</s>) foremost as an <s>agrahāra</s> by the people called <s>Kuru</s>, the inhabitants of this land — that too is <s>Kuruhāra</s>.
	In ancient times, the residents of this place bore the name <s>Kuru</s>.
	Since the grain and other wealth of this village was taken (<s>hriyate</s>) by them from the very beginning, it is also [called] <s>Kuruhāra</s>.
	Therefore, even by <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s>:
Thereafter, he became the giver of the <s>agrahāra</s> of <s>Kuruhāra</s>.

children.text:
iti kathanavaśād asya kuruhārāgrahāra iti samastaṃ nāma likhitam |
	yataḥ sarveṣām evāgrahārāṇāṃ sasyādisampatte rājagrāhya bhāgāt pūrvam eva nayanenāgrahāratvena vyapadeśaḥ |
	asya kuruhārapradeśasyādhunike kāle sarve grāmīṇāḥ svabhāṣāyāṃ kular iti sarvakāśmīrakaviditaṃ nāma kathayanti |
	ayaṃ kuruhāra vā kularākhyo grāmo dakṣiṇapārśve dacchunporpargaṇa ityākhyayā janaiḥ sarvataḥ kathyamāno vartate |
	asya kular grāmasya nikaṭe anyo 'pi grāmo 'tiprasiddho bhavati 'yam adhunā salar ityākhyayā janāḥ samastapuragaṇaprasiddhaṃ nāma vadanto dṛśyante |
	ubhāv evaitau kularsalar ityākhyau grāmau yātrikāṇām amareśvarayātrāyāṃ madhye mārgaṃ dṛggocaram āgacchataḥ |
	pratyutobhayor eva tīrthibhūtayor grāmayos teṣāṃ snānapūjādikartavyatāpy amareśvarayātrām atāśrayaṇenāsti |
	asyaiva kuruhārapradeśasyāpabhraṃśavaśāc cirakālāgatāt kular iti nāma sajjātam |
	kecit tu asya kuruhārākhyasya pradeśasya kāṭhus iti nāma kathayanti |
	tanmatena kāṭhus iti kular ity asyaiva cirakālāgatam apabhraṃśadoṣotthaṃ nāma bhavati |
	vastutas tu kuruhāraśabdasya kāṭhusśabdena tādṛśyaṃ sāmyam uccaraṇena jñāyate yādṛśaṃ tasya kularśabde na bhāti |
	atas samīcīnaṃ kular ity evāsya kuruhārasyāpabhraṃśadoṣotthaṃ nāma paraṃ tu ayaṃ kāṭhusākhyo grāmo 'py asminn eva dacchunporpargaṇe 'mareśvarayātrāmārgamadhye bhavati |
	yātrikāṇāṃ tatrāpy uktagrāmadvayaravasnānādikartavyatā bhavati |
	ataḥ salarkularākhyagrāmadvayanaikaṭyabhāg ayaṃ tṛtīyo grāmaḥ kuruhār iti vyapadiṣṭo bhrameṇaivāsti ||
children.translated_text: — thus, by way of this narration, the complete name '<s>Kuruhārāgrahāra</s>' has been written. For all <s>agrahāras</s> (tax-exempt Brahmanical endowments) are designated as <s>agrahāras</s> precisely because, prior to the king's receivable share from the produce of crops and the like, [the revenue] is taken away [for the endowment]. In modern times, all the villagers of this <s>Kuruhāra</s> region call it by the name 'Kular' in their own language, a name known to all Kashmiris. This village called <s>Kuruhāra</s> or 'Kular' is situated on the southern side, in what people everywhere call the 'Dacchunpor Pargaṇa' (Southern township). Near this village of 'Kular,' there is also another very famous village, which people are now seen calling by the name 'Salar,' a name well-known throughout the entire township. Both these villages called 'Kular' and 'Salar' come into the sight of pilgrims along the route of the <s>Amareśvara</s> pilgrimage. Indeed, in both these villages, which have become sacred sites (<s>tīrtha</s>), the duties of bathing, worship, and the like are obligatory for them as part of the <s>Amareśvara</s> pilgrimage. From this very <s>Kuruhāra</s> site, through long-standing phonetic corruption (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>), the name 'Kular' has arisen. Some, however, say the name of this <s>Kuruhāra</s> site is 'Kāṭhus.' According to that view, 'Kāṭhus,' like 'Kular,' is a name arising from long-standing phonetic corruption of [<s>Kuruhāra</s>]. But in truth, the similarity in pronunciation between the word '<s>Kuruhāra</s>' and the word 'Kāṭhus' is known to be [no greater] than [the similarity] that does not appear between it and the word 'Kular.' Therefore, the proper [conclusion is that] 'Kular' alone is the name arising from phonetic corruption of this '<s>Kuruhāra</s>.' However, this village called 'Kāṭhus' is also in this very 'Dacchunpor Pargaṇa,' along the route of the <s>Amareśvara</s> pilgrimage. For pilgrims there too, the duties of bathing at the aforementioned pair of villages obtain. Therefore, this third village, which is in the vicinity of the pair of villages called 'Salar' and 'Kular,' has been designated as '<s>Kuruhāra</s>' only through confusion.
18. <s>Khāgī</s>

children.text:
ślokasaṃ 90 namba 18 khagendrasya rājyavarṇane khāginirvacanam |
	atra khe ākāśe gacchatīti khagaḥ |
	khaga e[...]gaḥ |
	atha vā khe ākāśe āsamantād gacchatīti khāgaḥ |
	garuḍābhidho viṣṇor yānaṃ pakṣī khāgo vidyate yasya saḥ khāgī viṣṇuḥ |
	ayaṃ pradeśo viṣṇor murter adhiṣṭhanitvaṃ yato bibhārti |
	ata eva khāgīti tasya viṣṇor eva nāmnā prakhyātiṃ samāgataḥ |
	anyac ca etat pradeśanikaṭavartino garuḍanāmāṅkitasya garuḍāśramābhidhasya sthānasya sāmīpyena garuḍasya sadaiva viṣṇor vāhanatvena ca tatnāmnāpy ayaṃ prathāṃ prāpto 'taḥ khāgīti nāmāsya pradeśasya yuktatamaṃ bhāti |
	asmin khāgīti prathite grāme viṣṇoḥ pratimāyā adhiṣṭhānaṃ nārāyaṇakuṇḍeti sarvajanavidito madhyam aparīmāṇa eko jalāśayo bhavati |
	kāśmīrakās tu tasya nārāyaṇakuṇḍasyādhunike kāle svabhāṣayā nārāṇ nāg iti prathitaṃ nāma kathayanti |
	punaś ca yasyoktagaruḍāśramasya naikaṭyasattayāpy ayaṃ pradeśa enāṃ khāg ityākhyāṃ dhārayati |
	tasya garuḍāśramasyāpi yathā khāgīti pradeśasyāpabhraṃśadoṣotthaṃ khāg iti nāmadheyaṃ samudbhūtaṃ tathaiva tena doṣeṇa gaṇiśram iti nāma grāmīṇāḥ sarvato bruvāṇā bhavanti |
	ato varṇitam etat sthānadvayaṃ bahurūpa ityākhye puragaṇe tīrthībhūtam adhunāpy asti |
	asyāpi bahurūpapuragaṇasya grāmīṇaiḥ prakhyāpitaṃ bīrūpargaṇa iti nāmādhunike kāle saṃlagnam |
	asmin bahurūpākhye puragaṇe nārāyaṇakuṇḍādīnām etādṛśānāṃ tīrthānāṃ sadbhāvenaivātimāhātmyavattvaṃ sarvatra prasiddham asti |
	tathā ca nīlamate bahurūpe naraḥ snātvā viṣṇuloke mahīyate |
children.translated_text: Verse 90, number 18: the etymology of <s>Khāgī</s> in the description of the reign of <s>Khagendra</s>. Here, '<s>khaga</s>' means 'one who goes (<s>gacchati</s>) in the sky (<s>kha</s>, ākāśa).' [...] Or alternatively, '<s>khāga</s>' means 'one who goes everywhere in the sky.' <s>Garuḍa</s>, the bird who is <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s vehicle — he whose [emblem] is that <s>khāga</s> (sky-goer) is '<s>Khāgī</s>,' that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s>. This site bears the presiding presence of the image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. For this very reason, it has attained fame by the name '<s>Khāgī</s>,' [derived] from the name of that very <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Furthermore, due to its proximity to the place called <s>Garuḍāśrama</s> (the hermitage of <s>Garuḍa</s>), bearing the name of <s>Garuḍa</s>, which is situated nearby this site, and since <s>Garuḍa</s> is always <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s vehicle, this site has also gained fame by his name. Therefore the name '<s>Khāgī</s>' seems most fitting for this site. In this village known as '<s>Khāgī</s>,' the seat of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s image — a great, immeasurable water-body known to all people as <s>Nārāyaṇakuṇḍa</s> (the pool of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>) — exists in the middle [of the village]. The Kashmiris, in modern times, in their own language, call it by the well-known name 'Nārāṇ Nāg.' And further, due to its proximity to the aforementioned <s>Garuḍāśrama</s>, this site bears the name 'Khāg.' Just as this site '<s>Khāgī</s>' has the name 'Khāg' arising from phonetic corruption, so too, by the same corruption, the villagers everywhere are seen calling [<s>Garuḍāśrama</s>] 'Gaṇiśram.' Therefore, the two sites described here are in the township called '<s>Bahurūpa</s>' and remain sacred sites even today. This <s>Bahurūpa</s> township too has the name 'Bīrūpargaṇa' proclaimed by the villagers, attached [to it] in modern times. In this township called <s>Bahurūpa</s>, the supreme greatness and glory of such sacred sites as <s>Nārāyaṇakuṇḍa</s> and others is well established due to their very existence. And thus in the <s>Nīlamata</s> [Purāṇa]: 'Having bathed in <s>Bahurūpa</s>, a man is honored in <s>Viṣṇuloka</s> (the world of Viṣṇu).'

children.text: bahurūpe ca kathitaṃ phalam etan narottama ||
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Bahurūpa</s>, this fruit has been declared, O best of men.'

children.text:
ityādi |
	ayaṃ nārāyaṇ nāgākhyo jalāśayaś catuṣkoṇākāro 'tiśayena śītalasparśajalavās tathāmadhurāsvādaś ca bhavati |
	asya jalāśayasya mukhaṃ bṛhatpāṣāṇaiś catasṛṣv eva dikṣu ghaṭitam asti |
	ayaṃ pradeśaḥ svalpair marubhūmisadṛśaiḥ parvataiḥ prāptabhūmau parivṛto dṛśyate |
	ayam api khāgiti prācīnam eva nāma bibhrāṇo rājñāgrahāreti vyapadeśayutaḥ samapādita ity anumīyate ||
children.translated_text:
— and so forth.
	This water reservoir called <s>Nārāyaṇ Nāga</s> is square-shaped, and its water has an exceedingly cool touch and a sweet taste.
	The face [edges] of this reservoir are constructed with large stones on all four sides.
	This place is seen to be surrounded on the ground by small mountains resembling desert terrain.
	This [place], bearing the ancient name '<s>Khāgi</s>', is inferred to have been established with the designation '<s>Rājñā Grāhāra</s>' (a royal land-grant).
19. <s>Khonamuṣa</s>

children.text:
ślokasaṃ 90 namba 19 khagendrasya varṇane khonamuṣaḥ |
	asya niruktiḥ |
	kham indriyaṃ samākhyātaṃ kham ākāśe nigadyate |
	tathāṃśuke ca khaṃ proktaṃ khaṃ śūnyaṃ ca prakīrtitaṃ iti kośamatena |
	khair vastrair ūno rahito digambaraḥ śiva iti yāvat |
	taṃ khonaṃ śivaṃ parvatasthaguhāyāṃ muṣṇāti corayati yaḥ saḥ khonamuṣaḥ |
	atha vā khena śūnyo nono rahitaḥ paripūrṇaḥ pūrṇimācandras taṃ svakīyayā śītalayā manohāriṇyā ca śobhayā muṣṇāti yaḥ so 'pi khonamuṣaḥ |
	ayaṃ khonamuṣākhyaḥ pradeśaḥ parvatasya pādabhūmāv kham indriyaṃ samākhyātaṃ kham ākāśam udāhṛtam || khaṃ svarge ca samākhyātaṃ khaṃ sarpe ca prakīrtitam |
	tathā śvabhre ca khaṃ prāhuḥ khaṃ śūnye ca prakīrtitam || adhastād vartate |
	asminn evāsya parvatasyoparitane śikhare bṛhaty ekāntaḥ prakāśarahitā guhā vartate |
	tasyā guhāyā bhittibhūmiṣu parito devatānāṃ vaddhyo mūrtayaḥ saṃlakṣyante |
	tāsāṃ mūrtīnāṃ mukhyatamā ekā mahatī liṅgā kāravatī śivasya mūrtir harṣeśvara ityākhyāṃ sarvamaṇḍalaprakhyātāṃ dhārayantī bhūmau niṣarāṇā dṛśyate |
	asyā guhāyā antare 'nyālpāpy ekā guhāsti |
	tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ śivasya svacchandākhyā pañcabhir mukhair upaśobhitā mūrtir bahir eva darśanam āgacchati yatas tasyām alpāyāṃ guhāyāṃ praveśo 'pi sarvathā duṣkaro bhavati |
	pūrvaṃ bhasmāsurābhidhasyāsurasya vināśanavelāyāṃ śivena tasyoktadurjātāsurasya vañcanāyai kiṃcit kālaṃ svakīyā mūrtir asyāṃ guhāyāṃ guptatayā sthāpitā |
	atha taṃ duṣṭam asuraṃ vināśya yadātena mahān harṣabharaḥ samākalitas tadaiva tena devena harṣeśvara ityākhyā samāsāditā |
	ato 'sya pradeśasya guhayā śivamoṣaṇaṃ sārthakam evāvagamyate |
	grāmīṇā ādhunike kāle 'sya khonamuṣākhyapradeśasya khunamoh ityākhya śivamūrtibhedasya harimur iti nāmāpi vadantaḥ santi |
	asya harṣeśvarasya kathā harṣeśvaramāhātmye bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitāsaṅkalite vistareṇoktā bhavati |
	asya khonamoṣasya samīpe jayavanaṃ yasya kaśmīrabhāṣāyāṃ jivan iti nāma prasiddham asti |
	so 'pi grāmas tathānyo mābur ityākhyo grāmaś ca nikaṭe vartate |
	ayaṃ khunamuh ākhyo grāmaḥ vihī ityākhye puragaṇe prasiddhiṃ dhāryamāṇo bhavati |
	kaśmīranagarāt pañcakrośadūratāyāṃ grāmo 'yaṃ puragaṇaś cāstīti śam ||
children.translated_text:
Verse-collection [no.] 90, number 19: Description of <s>Khonamuṣa</s> [in the section] of <s>Khagendra</s>.
	Its etymology:
	'<s>Kha</s> is declared to mean "sense-organ"; <s>kha</s> is said [to mean] "sky"; likewise <s>kha</s> is said [to mean] "cloth"; and <s>kha</s> is declared [to mean] "void"' — according to the lexicon.
	'<s>Kha</s>' [means] cloth; '<s>ūna</s>' [means] devoid of — [hence] 'sky-clad' (<s>digambara</s>), that is to say, <s>Śiva</s>.
	He who steals (<s>muṣṇāti</s>) that <s>Khona</s> [i.e.,] <s>Śiva</s> in a cave on the mountain — that is '<s>Khonamuṣa</s>.'
	Alternatively: '<s>Khena</s>' [means] by void; '<s>ūna</s>' means devoid of, [hence] full — the full moon; he who steals [its beauty] by his own cool and captivating splendor — he too is '<s>Khonamuṣa</s>.'
	This place called <s>Khonamuṣa</s> is situated at the foot of the mountain. '<s>Kha</s> is declared to mean sense-organ; <s>kha</s> is said [to mean] sky; <s>kha</s> is declared [to mean] heaven; <s>kha</s> is declared [to mean] serpent; likewise they say <s>kha</s> [means] pit; and <s>kha</s> is declared [to mean] void' — [this place] lies below.
	On the very summit of this mountain, there is a large, solitary cave devoid of light.
	On the walls and floors of that cave, sculpted images of deities are observed all around.
	The foremost among those images is one great image of <s>Śiva</s> in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>, bearing the name '<s>Harṣeśvara</s>' — renowned throughout all regions — and is seen set into the ground.
	Within this cave, there is also another small cave.
	In that cave, an image of <s>Śiva</s> called <s>Svacchanda</s>, adorned with five faces, comes into view from outside, since entry into that small cave is altogether impossible.
	Formerly, at the time of the destruction of the demon called <s>Bhasmāsura</s>, <s>Śiva</s> had hidden his own image secretly in this cave for a while to deceive that wicked demon.
	Then, having destroyed that evil demon, when great joy was obtained by him, at that very time that god acquired the name '<s>Harṣeśvara</s>' ('Lord of Joy').
	Therefore, the 'stealing of <s>Śiva</s>' [implied] by the cave of this place is understood to be meaningful indeed.
	Villagers in modern times also speak of the name '<s>Harimur</s>' for a variant of the <s>Śiva</s> image [at this place] called <s>Khonamuṣa</s> [now called] '<s>Khunamoh</s>.'
	The story of this <s>Harṣeśvara</s> is told at length in the <s>Harṣeśvaramāhātmya</s> compiled in the <s>Bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā</s>.
	Near this <s>Khonamoṣa</s> is <s>Jayavana</s>, whose name in the Kashmiri language is well-known as '<s>Jivan</s>.'
	That village too, as well as another village called '<s>Mābur</s>,' are situated nearby.
	This village called '<s>Khunamuh</s>' holds fame in the district (<s>puragaṇa</s>) known as '<s>Vihī</s>.'
	This village and district are at a distance of five <s>krośa</s> from the city of <s>Kaśmīra</s> [Srinagar]. Thus all is well.
20. The <s>Darad</s> Country

children.translated_text:
Verse 93, number 20: Near the <s>Darad</s> country in the description of King <s>Surendra</s>'s reign.
	Therein, the etymology of <s>Daraddeśa</s>:
	The country (<s>deśa</s>) that is the dwelling-place of the communities (<s>janapadas</s>) of the <s>Darad</s> people, belonging to the <s>Dara</s> tribe.
	Many communities bearing the name <s>Darat</s> dwell in the mountains and borderlands surrounding the city of <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
	Many countries that serve as their dwelling-places have attained fame by the very name <s>Darad</s> in the border regions outside <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
	And in modern times, the people call that country inhabited by those <s>Dara</s>-tribe people by the name '<s>Dāradin hunu deś</s>' in the <s>Kaśmīra</s> language.
	And the well-known name of the inhabitants of that country is '<s>Dārady</s>' — this is universally known everywhere.
	Likewise, in the <s>Nīlamata</s> [Purāṇa] too:
The <s>Dārvas</s>, <s>Ābhisāras</s>, <s>Gāndhāras</s>, <s>Juhuṇḍas</s>, <s>Daras</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, and <s>Khaśas</s>,
the <s>Taṅganas</s>, <s>Māṇḍavas</s>, <s>Madras</s>, the inner-mountain and outer-mountain [peoples] —

children.text:
ity uktyā ya ete deśā janapadāśrayībhūtā gaṇitās te darajjātīyā evānumīyante |
	eteṣām anyeṣāṃ cāśrayasthānāni sarvāṇi daraddeśaśabdenaivābhidhīyante |
	ato 'yaṃ deśaḥ kaśmīrakarājñām ājñāsu sarvadaiva vidheyatayā tiṣṭhati |
	anenaiva hetunā kāśmīrako rājaiva daraddeśājñākṛt sarvadaivāstīty avagamyate ||
children.translated_text:
by this statement, all these countries that are enumerated as the dwelling-places of communities are inferred to be of the <s>Dara</s> tribe.
	The dwelling-places of these and others are all designated by the very word <s>Daraddeśa</s>.
	Therefore, this country always remains obedient to the commands of the kings of <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
	For this very reason, it is understood that only the king of <s>Kaśmīra</s> is always the commander of the <s>Darad</s> country.
21. The City of <s>Sauraka</s>

children.text:

	tathā hi
children.translated_text:
Verse 93, number 21: The town named <s>Sauraka</s> in the reign of <s>Surendra</s>.
	Therein, the etymology of the word <s>Sauraka</s>:
	'<s>Sa</s>' [means] 'anger' and 'prevention'; '<s>au</s>-sound' means also '<s>Brahma</s>'; '<s>aur</s>' too is said [to mean] 'bliss.' And '<s>ka</s>' is also called the self (<s>ātman</s>); '<s>ka</s>' denotes a region — thus, relying on these lexical statements: '<s>sa</s>' is the preventer, the protector from suffering; '<s>au</s>' is bliss; he who gives (<s>rāti</s>) that bliss is '<s>sora</s>.'
	Such a region (<s>ka</s>) is <s>Sauraka</s> — that is, a country that wards off suffering and bestows bliss.
	Alternatively, <s>saura</s> is 'the offspring of the sun (<s>sūrya</s>)' — that is, one resembling <s>Śani</s> (Saturn); a region that is like him — difficult to see due to its remoteness, dark and grimy due to being covered by forests, thickets, and the like, like <s>Śani</s> — that too is <s>Sauraka</s>.
	Such was the town (<s>pattana</s>), the city.
	'<s>Pattana</s>' means '<s>puṭabhedana</s>' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	Near the <s>Darad</s> country described earlier, the king <s>Surendra</s> established [this town] as a separate settlement — this is the meaning. It is understood by the very statement of <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s> that the city named <s>Sauraka</s> was independently established by the king in the <s>Darad</s> country, which is in the territory bordering the <s>Kaśmīra</s> region.
	Thus indeed:
Having established near the <s>Darad</s> country the town named <s>Sauraka</s>,
the glorious one established a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) called <s>Narendrabhava</s>.
And also:
By that <s>Khaṇḍayaśas</s>, [a king] of meritorious deeds, in his own territory,
a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), generous in good works, was built, named <s>Sorasa</s>.

children.text:
ity ādy ukteḥ svamaṇḍale kaśmīrākhye svamaṇḍalād anyatra daraddeśe ca rājño 'sya nirmāṇādikam abhūt |
	asya saurakākhyasya nagarasya kaśmīrabhāṣāyāṃ hasaur iti prathitatamaṃ nāma sarve kathayanti |
	vartate ca hasaurākhyaṃ nagaraṃ daraddeśe |
	daraddeśasyāpy asya dāradyan hundradeś vā dāradyan hundra mulak iti nāma prasiddham asti |
	punaś ca te ye haṇer gilgith hauja karṇāha ity ādayo deśāḥ kaśmīramaṇḍalāt pṛthaksthā api kaśmīrarājyāntar gaṇitā eva tathaitatmaṇḍalapālakasyājñāpālayamānāḥ sarvadaiva bhavanti |
	atas tasya rājño 'pi daraddeśe nagaranirmāṇam ucitatamaṃ bhavati |
	kecit tu pārisekānuvādavidaḥ saurakākhyam amuṃ pattanam ajānanto buddhibhrameṇa svakapolakalpitakalpanayā ca vṛthotthayā sindhaṣurath ityākhyaṃ kam api pradeśaṃ saurakaśabdābhidheyaṃ parikalpya rājño sindhuṣurathākhyo deśo nirmita ityādi likhanti |
	tat sarvaṃ teṣāṃ likhanam asatyatamam asti |
	yato rājataraṅgiṇyukte surendrasya varṇane kim apy etādṛśaṃ deśanirmāṇaṃ kvāpi na dṛṣṭam |
	ato 'tra prayojanam ajñātvaiva tanmatam astīti budhyate ||
children.translated_text:
— thus and such is the statement. In his own territory called <s>Kaśmīra</s>, and also in the <s>Darad</s> country outside his own territory, construction and the like by this king took place.
	The most well-known name of this city called <s>Sauraka</s> in the <s>Kaśmīra</s> language, as everyone says, is '<s>Hasaur</s>.'
	And the city called <s>Hasaur</s> exists in the <s>Darad</s> country.
	The well-known name of this <s>Darad</s> country too is '<s>Dāradyan Hundradeś</s>' or '<s>Dāradyan Hundra Mulak</s>.'
	Furthermore, those countries called <s>Haṇer</s>, <s>Gilgith</s>, <s>Hauja</s>, <s>Karṇāha</s>, and others — although situated separately from the <s>Kaśmīra</s> territory, they are counted within the <s>Kaśmīra</s> kingdom and always remain obedient to the orders of the governor of this territory.
	Therefore, it is most appropriate that this king too constructed a city in the <s>Darad</s> country.
	However, certain scholars of the Persian translation, not knowing this city called <s>Sauraka</s>, through intellectual confusion and a fabricated invention of their own imagination, imagining some place called '<s>Sindhaṣurath</s>' to be designated by the word <s>Sauraka</s>, write that 'a country called <s>Sindhuṣurath</s> was built by the king' and so on.
	All of their writing is most untrue.
	Because in the account of <s>Surendra</s> as stated in the <s>Rājataraṅgiṇī</s>, no such construction of a country is seen anywhere.
	Therefore, it is understood that their opinion exists without even knowing the purpose here.
22. The <s>Vihāra</s> (Buddhist Monastery) Named <s>Narendrabhavana</s>

children.text:

	atra narendrabhavanaśabdasya niruktiḥ |
	narāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇām indro rājā narendraḥ |
	narendrasya bhavanaṃ gṛhaṃ narendrabhavanaṃ rājagṛham ity arthaḥ |

	gaṃjā tu madirāgṛham ity amaraḥ |
	tādṛśaṃ bauddhamandiram api nirmitam |

children.translated_text:
Verse 93, number 22: The <s>vihāra</s> (Buddhist monastery) named <s>Narendrabhavana</s> in the reign of King <s>Surendra</s>.
	Herein, the etymology of the word <s>Narendrabhavana</s>:
	The <s>Indra</s> (lord) of <s>naras</s> (men), that is, the king of men, is <s>Narendra</s>.
	The <s>bhavana</s> (dwelling) of <s>Narendra</s> is <s>Narendrabhavana</s> — meaning the royal palace.
	Just as kings have their own residences constructed by craftsmen, inlaid with gold, silver, gems, and the like in the purest manner, so too by King <s>Surendra</s>, having built a city called <s>Hasaur</s> near the <s>Darad</s> country, right there the <s>vihāra</s> named <s>Narendrabhavana</s> — meaning a dwelling useful for Buddhists — was [built].
	'A dwelling useful for Buddhists — for Buddhists, a <s>vihāra</s> is feminine;
	a <s>gaṃjā</s> (distillery) is a liquor-house' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	Such a Buddhist temple was also built.
	And near this city called <s>Hasaur</s>, situated in the midst of the <s>Darad</s> country, there exists a place named <s>Narendrabhavana</s>.
	The well-known name of that <s>Narendrabhavana</s> in modern times, according to the Kashmiris, is '<s>Nagūr</s>.'
	Since that place called <s>Nagūr</s> is situated right near <s>Hasaur</s>, therefore this very place designated by the word <s>Narendrabhavana</s> shines.
	In just this way, the king's construction in the <s>Darad</s> country at the places called <s>Hasaur</s> and <s>Nagūr</s>, [and] in his own territory the construction of [other] places, will be described further ahead.
23. The <s>Vihāra</s> (Buddhist Monastery) of <s>Sorasa</s>

children.text:
śloka 94 namba 23 surendrasya rājye sorasābhidhaḥ vihāraḥ |
	tatra pūrvaṃ sorasaśabdaniruktiḥ |
	saḥ kope vāraṇe caiveti kośokteḥ |
	sovāraka ūṣpādeḥ pipāsādeś ca tathā ukāraḥ śaṅkare prokta ūkāraś caiva rakṣake iti kośokteś ca |
	ū rakṣako jīvanam iti yāvat |
	tathā ca raso gandharase jale śṛṅgārādau viṣe vīrye tiktādau dravarāgayoḥ dehadhātuprabhede ca pāradasvādayoḥ pumān iti medinīkośamatāvalambanena |
	raso jalaṃ yasya saḥ sorasaḥ |
	atra rasaśabdasya jīvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ vanam ity amaramatena |
	jalaparyāyeṇa jīvanaśabdena saha samānārthatvād rakṣakajīvanaśabdayoś ca tulyārthatayā rakṣakatvaviśeṣaṇaṃ samīcīnam evāsti |
	ato gharmādivārakajalavānayavihārasaṃjñabauddhamandirayutaḥ pradeśa ity arthaḥ |
	ādhunike kāle 'sya sorasākhyasya pradeśasya kaśmīrabhāṣayā suras yār iti nāma grāmīṇāḥ kathayanti |
	asmin pradeśe dugdhagaṅgākhyā nadī śītalasparśā madhurāsvādajalā pārvāyatrī ca pravahati |
	ataḥ soraseti sārthakaṃ nāmāsya eṣā yā dugdhagaṅgākhyā nadī dhārayati |
	asyāḥ kāśmīrakā dūdgaṅgā iti prathitaṃ nāmāsti |
	anyad ayaṃ sorasākhyaḥ pradeśo nāgom ityākhye puragaṇe vartate |
	tatrāpi parvatasya pādadeśo bhavati |
	asya sorasasya nikaṭe ḍāḍa um pūr tathā mici um pūr ityākhyaṃ grāmadvayaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text:
Verse 94, number 23: The <s>vihāra</s> (Buddhist monastery) named <s>Sorasa</s> in the reign of <s>Surendra</s>.
	First, the etymology of the word <s>Sorasa</s>:
	'<s>Sa</s>' [means] 'anger' and 'prevention,' according to the lexicon.
	'<s>So</s>' [is from] '<s>vāraka</s>' (protector); '<s>ū</s>' [is from] 'heat' and 'thirst' and so forth; and '<s>u</s>' is declared [to mean] '<s>Śaṅkara</s>' (Śiva), and '<s>ū</s>' [means] 'protector,' according to the lexicon.
	'<s>Ū</s>' means protector, that is, life-sustaining.
	And furthermore, relying on the <s>Medinī</s> lexicon [which states]: '<s>rasa</s>' [means] 'fragrance,' 'juice,' 'water,' 'the erotic sentiment and the like,' 'poison,' 'potency,' 'bitter and other [tastes],' 'liquid,' 'attachment,' 'a variety of bodily constituent,' 'mercury,' and 'flavor' — [all these being] masculine.
	That which has water (<s>rasa</s>) is <s>Sorasa</s>.
	Here, the word '<s>rasa</s>' [is synonymous with] 'life' (<s>jīvana</s>), 'world' (<s>bhuvana</s>), and 'forest' (<s>vana</s>), according to <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	Since the word '<s>jīvana</s>' is synonymous with water, and the words 'protector' (<s>rakṣaka</s>) and 'life-sustaining' (<s>jīvana</s>) have equivalent meaning, the qualification of 'protective nature' is entirely fitting.
	Therefore, the meaning is: a region endowed with a Buddhist temple called a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), possessing water that wards off heat and the like.
	In modern times, the villagers call this region named <s>Sorasa</s> by the name '<s>Suras Yār</s>' in the Kashmiri language.
	In this region flows a river called <s>Dugdhagaṅgā</s> (Milk-Ganges), cool to the touch, with sweet-tasting water, and flowing eastward.
	Therefore, the name <s>Sorasa</s> is meaningful — this river called <s>Dugdhagaṅgā</s> bears [witness to] it.
	Its well-known name among the Kashmiris is '<s>Dūdgaṅgā</s>.'
	Furthermore, this region called <s>Sorasa</s> is situated in the district called <s>Nāgom</s>.
	There too it lies at the foot of the mountain.
	Near this <s>Sorasa</s>, there are two villages called <s>Ḍāḍa Um Pūr</s> and <s>Mici Um Pūr</s>.
24. The <s>Agrahāra</s> (land-grant) named <s>Hastiśālā</s>

children.text:

	tatra hastiśālākhyaśabdanirvacanam |
	hastino śālante śobhante 'treti gajāḥ hastiśālam |
	śālante iti śālyaślāghāyām iti dhāto rūpam |
	atha vā hastināṃ śālā hastiśālā hastināṃ gṛhaṃ nivasanasthānam iti yāvat |
	etādṛśam agrahāraṃ godhareṇa rājñā nirmitaṃ nirmāya ca viprebhyo dattam ity arthaḥ |

Verse 96, number 24: The <s>agrahāra</s> (land-grant) named <s>Hastiśālā</s> in the description of King <s>Godhara</s>.
	Therein, the etymology of the word <s>Hastiśālā</s>:
	Elephants (<s>hastinas</s>) shine (<s>śālante</s>) here — hence [it is called] <s>Hastiśāla</s>. '<s>Śālante</s>' is a form of the root '<s>śāl</s>' meaning 'to praise.'
	Alternatively, the hall (<s>śālā</s>) of elephants (<s>hastins</s>) is <s>Hastiśālā</s> — that is, the dwelling-place, the residence of elephants.
	Such an <s>agrahāra</s> was constructed by King <s>Godhara</s> and, having constructed it, was given to the Brahmins — this is the meaning.
	The intent here is: since the place designated for maintaining the rut-maddened elephants, she-elephants, and young elephants that were in the king's household was fixed in this very region, therefore the name <s>Hastiśāla</s> ('elephant stable') became attached to this region.
	There exists a village named <s>Hastiśālā</s> in the district called <s>Devasaras</s>.
	And the modern vernacular name of the district called <s>Devasaras</s> is '<s>Devasarpargaṇa</s>.'
	Furthermore, the universally known name of this village called <s>Hastiśālā</s> is also '<s>Hasty Hel</s>.'
	Near this village of <s>Hasty Hel</s> is a village called <s>Kulagrāma</s>.
	People now call it by the name '<s>Kulgom</s>,' considering it the principal village and administrative seat of the entire <s>Devasarpargaṇa</s> district.
	That village is nearby.
	Some say that the extremely famous great lake called <s>Ḍal</s>, known to all Kashmiris, situated in the <s>Phāk</s> district, on whose banks many greatly renowned gardens such as <s>Niśātbāg</s> and <s>Śālabāg</s> are still visible even today —
	on one bank of that very lake there is a place called by this name '<s>Hasty Hel</s>,' they say.
	However, even though a place called <s>Hastiśālā</s> certainly does exist on the bank of the lake called <s>Ḍal</s>, at some distance from the foremost renowned spot on that bank called '<s>Haj Ratabal</s>' and near the place called '<s>Āśiyabāg</s>' there, nevertheless, since this [lakeside] <s>Hastiśālā</s> is mostly water, since there is no space for any meaningful purpose, since it could not possibly serve as an elephant stable, and since being mostly water it is unworthy of being granted to Brahmins — it is that very <s>agrahāra</s> named <s>Hastiśālā</s> situated in the midst of the <s>Devasaras</s> district, constructed by King <s>Godhara</s>, that shines [as the true one].
	Not this other mostly-water place named <s>Hastiśālā</s>, unworthy of the designation of <s>agrahāra</s>.
	Moreover, in the Persian translation as well, the construction of the <s>agrahāra</s> by King <s>Godhāra</s> is recorded as being that of <s>Hastiśālā</s> originating from <s>Devasaras</s>,
	not this other one belonging to the <s>Phāk</s> district. Thus all is well.

Verse 97, number 25: <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s> in the description of the reign of <s>Suvarṇa</s>.
	Therein, the etymology of the word <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s>:
	That which has a beautiful (<s>su</s>) color (<s>varṇa</s>) is <s>suvarṇa</s> — gold. '<s>Kāñcana</s>,' '<s>svarṇa</s>,' '<s>suvarṇa</s>,' '<s>kanaka</s>' [are synonyms]. And <s>maṇi</s> means gem:
	'<s>Ratna</s>' and '<s>maṇi</s>' [apply] to both [classes]; in the category of stones and in pearls and such — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	A <s>kulyā</s> (canal) of gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>) and gems (<s>maṇi</s>) — a small, man-made river.
	'<s>Kulyā</s>' means a small, man-made river — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	The meaning is: the river named <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s> was created by the king named <s>Suvarṇa</s>.
	Here, the banks and bed of which were adorned and constructed with gold and gems — such a river was set in motion by him.
	Alternatively, upon careful examination, it is understood that the name of this river is meaningful indeed: it is a river whose water is pure in color like gold and crystal-clear and captivating like gems.
	Here:
His son, named <s>Suvarṇa</s>, thereafter became a giver of gold to supplicants,
he who was the initiator of the <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s> canal, [flowing] through the gorge.

children.translated_text:
Thus says <s>Paṇḍita Kalhaṇa</s>.
	In the description of <s>Suvarṇa</s>'s reign, having mentioned <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s>, what he writes:
	The understanding that naturally arises in the mind is that this <s>kulyā</s> (canal) must necessarily have its course in a place called <s>Karāla</s>.
	However, in the entire <s>pargaṇa</s> (district) through which this river flows even today, despite searching with great effort and exertion, no place or village named <s>Karāla</s> is found anywhere.
	Therefore, the understanding that the <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s> flowed in a place called <s>Karāla</s> appears to be merely a misconception born of error.
	But examining the truth, the intention of the poet <s>Kalhaṇa</s> can be inferred as follows:
	According to the <s>Amarakośa</s>, '<s>karāla</s>' means 'jagged' or 'rough' (<s>danturaṃ turaḥ</s>).
	Any place that is very high (<s>atituṅga</s>) can be designated by the word <s>karāla</s>.
	Thus indeed, the understanding that the king caused the river to flow in a high (<s>tuṅga</s>) place called <s>karāla</s> appears most fitting.
	Since this river exists in the <s>Ādyāvanī</s> land, which is higher than all other lands of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, the poet's statement that the river was made to flow from the high ground synonymous with <s>karāla</s> is entirely consistent.
	In this <s>Kaśmīra</s>, when in ancient times it existed in the form of a lake and there was no land anywhere, then by the grace of the triad of deities propitiated by the sage <s>Kaśyapa</s>, wherever land first emerged, that very land received the meaningful name '<s>Ādyāvanī</s>' (the primordial earth).
	Because '<s>ādyā</s>' means 'existing from the beginning,' and '<s>avanī</s>' or '<s>avanī</s>' means 'earth' — that is the meaning.
	The <s>Amarakośa</s> states: '<s>kṣmā</s>, <s>avanī</s>, <s>medinī</s>, <s>mahī</s>.'
	And the <s>Medinīkośa</s>: '<s>avanī</s>, <s>medinī</s>, <s>mahī</s>.'
	Thus in every way the name <s>Ādyāvanī</s> for this <s>pargaṇa</s> is meaningful.
	The name of this <s>Ādyāvanī</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> as proclaimed by townspeople and villagers in modern times is '<s>Āḍavin Pargaṇa</s>' — this is rooted in the corruption (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>) of the name.
	This river called <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s>, celebrated in the reign of King <s>Suvarṇa</s> — its universally known name is '<s>Sunamaṇ Kul</s>' or '<s>Sunamaṇ Nor</s>.'
	In the first interpretation, the meaning is: the river (<s>kul</s>) named <s>Sunamaṇ</s>.
	In the second, the meaning is: the canal (<s>nor</s>, water-channel) named <s>Sunamaṇ</s>.
	Regarding both, the <s>Amarakośa</s> states: '<s>praṇālī</s> means a watercourse.'
	However, since this river called <s>Suvarṇamaṇikulyā</s> does not flow through just one village of this <s>pargaṇa</s>, it has no single fixed location.
	In many villages of this <s>pargaṇa</s>, the production of crops and such is made possible by the water of this river called <s>Sunamaṇ</s>.
	In the irrigation records too, they describe that in this <s>Ādyāvanī</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> itself, the king caused the <s>Sunamaṇ</s> river to flow, with the intention that the prosperity of crops and fruits of the villages situated there would endure forever, and so on.
	For this reason too, the flowing of the river in a place called <s>Karāla</s> appears entirely meaningless, since even they could not find any place called <s>Karāla</s> in their own descriptions.
	Therefore, in whatever way, the intention of the poet <s>Kalhaṇa</s>, who was skilled in suggestion (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), was to describe the <s>Ādyāvanī</s> land by the word <s>karāla</s>. May there be well-being.

Verse 98, number 26: The <s>vihāra</s> (Buddhist monastery) and <s>agrahāra</s> (land-grant) named <s>Jālora</s> in the description of <s>Janaka</s>, son of <s>Suvarṇa</s>.
	Here, the etymology of the word <s>Jālora</s>:
	By flower-garlands (<s>puṣpajāla</s>), '<s>ū</s>' means protector from foul odors and such — hence '<s>jālo</s>'; and '<s>ra</s>' means that which gives pleasure — thus '<s>Sujālora</s>.' '<s>Ū</s>' means protector, according to the lexicon.
	Alternatively, a collection (<s>samūha</s>) of waters (<s>jala</s>) is '<s>jāla</s>'; by that <s>jāla</s>, '<s>ū</s>' is the protector and '<s>ra</s>' is the giver of happiness.
	In this very region called <s>Jālora</s>, a Buddhist temple called a <s>vihāra</s> was constructed by that king, and this same [place] was proclaimed as the <s>agrahāra</s> of <s>Jālora</s>.
	The villagers say that the well-known name of this village of <s>Jālora</s> in modern times is '<s>Jālur</s>.'
	This village of <s>Jālur</s> is situated in the <s>Śamālā</s> district.
	The name of the district called <s>Śamālā</s> has been established as '<s>Hamalpargaṇa</s>' by the people themselves, due to the corruption of the word.
	This village of <s>Jālur</s> is sometimes seen being flooded by the waters of <s>Mahāpadmasaras</s> (the great Padma lake) or of the <s>Ullola</s> <s>nāga</s> (serpent-deity); therefore, due to the presence of a mass of water, the description '<s>jāla</s>' meaning 'a collection of waters' is most fitting for this region.
	Near this village of <s>Jālur</s>, many villages such as <s>Uccha</s>, <s>Kuṇḍal</s>, <s>Markuṇḍal</s>, and others are in proximity. Thus all is well.

	Here, the etymology of the word <s>Śamāṅgāsa</s>:
	The cessation of the mind from various intentions, doubts, and such is '<s>śama</s>' (tranquility), since the root '<s>śam</s>' meaning 'to be calm' (<s>upaśama</s>) conveys cessation.
	And those whose limbs (<s>aṅga</s>) are tranquil (<s>śamavanti</s>) — they are peaceful sages, designated by the word '<s>śamāṅga</s>.' Those very '<s>śamāṅgas</s>' sit (<s>āsante</s>)
	where — that is <s>Śamāṅgāsa</s>: the dwelling-place of peaceful sages.
	This region exists adorned by wild trees such as pines (<s>sarala</s>) and the like, hence it is predominantly forest, marked by asceticism, and suitable for <s>tapas</s> (austerities).
	The entire district called <s>Kuṭahāra</s> in which this region is situated appears always mostly enveloped by forest regions.
	Therefore, 'enchanting (<s>hāra</s>) by mountain peaks (<s>kūṭa</s>)' is indeed a meaningful name for this district. In modern times, everyone calls it by the well-known name '<s>Kuṭahārpargaṇa</s>.'
	The well-known name of this region of <s>Śamāṅgāsa</s> in the present day is '<s>Śāṅgās</s>,' a name arising from the corruption of the word.
	This village called <s>Śāṅgās</s> is situated on the ground level at the base of a small mountain.
	Since the beauty and form of this region is just like that of the other forests situated in this <s>Kaśmīra</s>, therefore the indicative and meaningful name of this place is 'the dwelling-place of sages.'
	In this region, all residents of good name and standing, always going back and forth for hunting and such purposes, are seen engaging in the chase — hence this region is most renowned, one should know.
	Many well-known villages near this region of <s>Śāṅgās</s> include <s>Navgām</s>, <s>Utarus</s>, <s>Cerapor</s>, and others.
	Furthermore, this village called <s>Śamāṅgāsa</s>, although already deemed suitable by sages for performing austerities as their dwelling-place, was designated by that prince <s>Janakaja</s> (son of <s>Janaka</s>) with the title of principal <s>agrahāra</s>.
	That is, [it was] offered to the ascetics residing in that region. This entire district, being dear to ascetics and a place for austerities, [continues thus] — even today in villages such as <s>Utarus</s> and others, there exist ascetics marked with the name '<s>Nand</s>,' who are disciples of those ancient ascetics, whose lineage continues even now through disciples and grand-disciples. Thus all is well.
28. <s>Aśanāra</s>

children.text:
śloka 100 namba 28 asyaiva śacīnarasya varṇane aśanāraḥ |
	tatrāsya niruktiḥ |
	aśyate bhujyate yat tad aśanaṃ bhojanam aśabhojane ity asya dhātor lyuṭi rūpam |

	aśanāyā bubhukṣā kṣud ity amaraḥ |

children.translated_text:
Verse 100, number 28: <s>Aśanāra</s> in the description of this same <s>Śacīnara</s>.
	Therein, the etymology of this [word]:
	That which is eaten (<s>aśyate</s>) or consumed (<s>bhujyate</s>) is <s>aśana</s> (food) — it is a <s>lyuṭ</s> form of the root <s>aś</s> (to eat).
	The desire for food (<s>aśana</s>) is <s>aśanāyā</s>, meaning hunger (<s>kṣud</s>).
	'<s>Aśanāyā</s>' is hunger (<s>bubhukṣā</s>), meaning '<s>kṣud</s>' — thus says the <s>Amarakośa</s>.
	And thus, <s>aśanāyā</s> itself is <s>aśanā</s>; he who gives (<s>rāti</s>, <s>dadāti</s>) that <s>aśanā</s> (hunger) completely (<s>ā samantāt</s>) is <s>Aśanāra</s>.
	The water that flows in this region, due to its extremely digestive quality, has the capacity to digest the four types of food that has been consumed.
	All the inhabitants there acknowledge this.
	Therefore, the capacity to produce hunger (<s>bubhukṣā</s>) appears to be the very meaningful significance of the name <s>Aśanāra</s>.
	This region called <s>Aśanāra</s> is situated in the <s>pargaṇa</s> called <s>Vyūha</s>.
	And the name of this <s>pargaṇa</s> called <s>Vyūha</s>, as declared by the villagers, is <s>Vihīpargaṇa</s>.
	People everywhere are seen calling this region also by the name <s>Śār</s>.
	In this village of <s>Śār</s>, there is also an iron mine.
	From certain special stones from which iron is produced through smelting and similar processes, there also exists a mountain characterized by those very stones.
	Therefore, the water of this village that originates from the iron mine is necessarily the most digestive in all places.
	Hence, the name <s>Aśanāra</s> is entirely meaningful for this village.
	Near this village of <s>Śār</s>, there is a well-known village called <s>Maṇḍikhpāl</s>, and another village called <s>Luḍhav</s> is also nearby.
29. <s>Śuṣkaletra</s>

children.text:

	śuṣkāni śoṣaṃ prāptāni tṛṇaparṇādīni lāti ādatte iti śuṣkalo vāyuḥ |
	lā ādāne ity asya dhāto rūpaṃ |
	tathā ca lakṣmīr īkāra ucyate iti kośāt |
	īr lakṣmī śuṣkalasya īḥ sampattiḥ śuṣkale vāyusampat |
	mahān vāyusamūha iti yāvat |
	tāṃ śuṣkale vāyusampattiṃ trāyate iti śuṣkaletraḥ traiṅ pālane dhātur atra |
	yato 'yaṃ pradeśo marubhūmistho 'ta eva mahatyā vānyayāyuta ity arthaḥ |
	ayam eva pradeśas tena rājñāśokena stūpapadavācyair bauddhānāṃ devāyatanair ācchāditaḥ |

	asmin sarvasminn eva puragaṇe sarvatra marubhūmisthe vāyoḥ pracalato 'nyabhūmibhya uccaistvenādhikyaṃ yato bhavaty ata eva śuṣkaletra iti vāyor ādhikyasadbhāvopalakṣitam anvartham eva nāmeti śam ||
children.translated_text:
Verse 102, number 29: <s>Śuṣkaletra</s> in the description of King <s>Aśoka</s>.
	Therein, the etymology of <s>Śuṣkaletra</s>:
	That which takes up (<s>lāti</s>, <s>ādatte</s>) dried (<s>śuṣka</s>) things — grass, leaves, and the like — that have reached a state of desiccation (<s>śoṣa</s>) — is <s>śuṣkala</s>, meaning the wind (<s>vāyu</s>).
	'<s>Lā</s>' in the sense of taking — this is a form of that root.
	And thus, from the lexicon: '<s>lakṣmī</s>' is called '<s>ī</s>-sound (<s>īkāra</s>)' [i.e., prosperity].
	'<s>Īr</s>' is <s>Lakṣmī</s>; the '<s>ī</s>' of <s>śuṣkala</s> is prosperity (<s>sampatti</s>); the prosperity of <s>śuṣkala</s> is an abundance of wind (<s>vāyusampat</s>),
	meaning a great mass of wind.
	He who protects (<s>trāyate</s>) that abundance of wind (<s>vāyusampatti</s>) of <s>śuṣkala</s> is <s>Śuṣkaletra</s> — the root '<s>trai</s>' in the sense of protecting is used here.
	Since this region is situated in arid land (<s>marubhūmi</s>), it is thus endowed with a great windstorm — that is the meaning.
	This very region was covered by King <s>Aśoka</s> with Buddhist temples, referred to by the term <s>stūpa</s>.
	The name of this region called <s>Śuṣkaletra</s>, as declared by the villagers in modern times, is <s>Hukhalitar</s>.
	This village called <s>Hukhalitar</s> is located in the <s>pargaṇa</s> named <s>Daiñcho</s>.
	This <s>pargaṇa</s> is situated at a distance of four <s>krośas</s> from the city of <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
	Near this village of <s>Hukhalitar</s>, there are villages such as <s>Śīlypūr</s> and others.
	Since in this entire <s>pargaṇa</s>, which is everywhere situated on arid land, the blowing wind is in greater excess compared to other lands — hence the name <s>Śuṣkaletra</s>, marked by the abundance of wind, is indeed meaningful. May there be well-being.
30. <s>Vitastātra</s>

children.text:

children.translated_text:
Verse number 102, number 30: <s>Vitastātra</s> in the reign of <s>Aśoka</s>.
	Here, the etymology of <s>Vitastātra</s>:
	According to the statement of the <s>Amarakośa</s>: 'From the thumb to the little finger is a <s>vitasti</s> (span), measuring twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths).'
	For every person, twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> measured by one's own proportions are denoted by the word <s>vitasti</s>.
	The river that is measured by that <s>vitasti</s> measure is called <s>Vitastā</s>.
	Accordingly, in the <s>Nīlamata</s> [Purāṇa], in the description of the manifestation of Goddess <s>Satī</s> in the form of the <s>Vitastā</s>, [the sage] <s>Bṛhadaśva</s> [narrates]: 'Having learned the truth, she, shaken with supreme patience, the Goddess with a face beautiful as the moon, said to her husband: "I shall take the form of a river in the netherworld, O Teacher of the World. Strike with the trident near the <s>Nīlaveśma</s> (Blue House). With the plough-point that was previously used by the Lord for splitting the mountain, by that trident-strike I shall emerge from the netherworld and travel along the trident's path as far as the great river <s>Sindhu</s>."
	When <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva) did so, the auspicious <s>Satī</s> acted accordingly.
	<s>Śaṅkara</s> himself gave her the name <s>Vitastā</s>.
	<s>Hara</s> made a pit measuring only one <s>vitasti</s> with the trident.
	That excellent river emerged through it from the netherworld; therefore the name <s>Vitastā</s> was given to her
	by the Self-born One. Then in all lands the news spread that <s>Maheśvarī</s> (the Great Goddess) had arisen, and out of love for the sage, she again purified the land.
	In those various lands, the people heard with eagerness that Goddess <s>Satī</s>, having become a river, had emerged from <s>Kaśmīra</s>.' By this narration, it is established that the name <s>Vitastā</s> for this river is indeed etymologically meaningful.
	However, it should be understood that in the <s>vitasti</s> measure, these twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> are those of a man twenty-five years of age.
	That which protects (<s>trāyate</s>) this described <s>Vitastā</s> as a mine and as a place of sovereignty,
	and which also brings water-filling in the form of a current — that is <s>Vitastātra</s>.
	Here too, the verbal root is <s>trai</s> (to protect), as before.
	In this place called <s>Vitastātra</s>, where the river had not become a mine, although only a few years ago in the past, only a pit measuring one <s>vitasti</s> was observed, nevertheless now a great reservoir created by the ruler of <s>Kaśmīra</s> named the glorious <s>Raṇavīrasiṃha</s> dwelling in heaven is seen.
	However, before the time of this king's new construction and restoration of old [structures], there was only a pit measuring twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>.
	Therefore, the statements in the <s>Nīlamata Purāṇa</s>, the <s>Vitastāmāhātmya</s>, and such texts that describe the measure of the river appear consistent and appropriate.
	The modern name of this place called <s>Vitastātra</s>, as spoken by townspeople and villagers, is '<s>Vithavatur</s>.'
	Therein, '<s>vith</s>' means 'of <s>Vitastā</s>' and '<s>vatur</s>' means 'source' — thus the meaning is consistent even in the <s>Kaśmīra</s> language.
	This village called <s>Vithavatur</s> is situated at the junction of two <s>pargaṇas</s> (districts) called <s>Śāhūbād</s> and <s>Devasaras</s>.
	Of these, the <s>Śāhūbād</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> is also known as <s>Śrīraṇavīrasiṃghapur</s>, and this <s>Devasaras</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> is also known as <s>Divāsar Pargaṇa</s> — everyone speaks both these names in modern times.
	Certain authors of irrigation records write the name of this place called <s>Vitastātra</s> as '<s>Vatarahel</s>' in their books.
	That village called <s>Vatarahel</s> is situated in a <s>pargaṇa</s> called <s>Daiñcho</s>.
	Therefore, this <s>Śuṣkaletra</s>,
	or the village called <s>Hukhalitar</s> described earlier — since it is mentioned together with this <s>Vitastātra</s>,
	or with the village <s>Vithavatur</s>, and since one and the same king named <s>Aśoka</s> was the builder of both places, those who mistakenly consider this <s>Vitastātra</s> to be situated in the <s>Daiñcho</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> like <s>Śuṣkaletra</s> establish <s>Vitastātra</s> as '<s>Vatarahel</s>' according to their own view.
	But since in the entire <s>Daiñcho</s> <s>pargaṇa</s> even the name of <s>Vitastā</s> does not exist, how can we call <s>Vitastātra</s> by the name '<s>Vatarahel</s>'?
	Therefore, their writing appears to be merely a fabrication of their own imagination — let that be.
	Certain other followers of that view, mistakenly considering this place called <s>Vitastātra</s> to be '<s>Vithanār</s>' and different from the <s>Vatarahel</s> area, are seen calling this <s>Vitastātra</s> by the name '<s>Vithanār</s>.'
	Therein, '<s>vith</s>' means 'of <s>Vitastā</s>' and '<s>nār</s>' means 'canal' — that is the meaning.
	This place called <s>Vithanār</s> is situated one <s>krośa</s> (about 2 miles) from the city of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, on the bank of the <s>Vitastā</s> river.
	Here the elders say: in former times, when every year this <s>Vitastā</s> river, being filled by masses of water from rising floods, used to make this entire region liable to flooding, then the rulers of <s>Kaśmīra</s> at that time ordered craftsmen to create a canal-like channel.
	By those very craftsmen, a canal-channel was created that prevented the danger of flooding from rising waters.
	To that very canal, the name '<s>Vithanār</s>' became attached in the manner described.
	Here, from the poet <s>Kalhaṇa</s>'s statement mentioning '<s>Śuṣkaletra</s>, <s>Vitastātra</s>, <s>stūpa</s>-circles' and so on, both this place called <s>Vatarahel</s> and this place called <s>Vithanār</s>
	appear unworthy of being covered by a Buddhist temple (<s>stūpa</s>) denoted by the word <s>stūpa</s>.
	The first, <s>Vatarahel</s>, because it has no connection to the <s>Vitastā</s> river, making the name <s>Vitastātra</s> most inappropriate for it;
	the second, <s>Vithanār</s>, because it consists of a canal-channel and is [also unsuitable as] a foundation for a <s>stūpa</s>.
	Therefore, it is established that this village <s>Vithavatur</s> alone is denoted by the word <s>Vitastātra</s>,
	since only it has the possibility of being a foundation for a <s>stūpa</s>, and not any other. May there be well-being.
31. <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> <s>Vihāra</s> (The Forest of Dharma Monastery)

children.text:

children.translated_text:
Verse 103, number 31: In the reign of the aforementioned <s>Aśoka</s>, the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) that was built within the <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s> (Forest of Dharma Monastery) at <s>Vitastātra</s> city.
	First, the etymology of the word <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s>:
	<s>Dharma</s> is the collection of actions approved by good scholars free from passion and hatred, [...] which accomplishes heaven, liberation, and the like.
	The forest (<s>araṇya</s>) of <s>dharma</s> is <s>Dharmāraṇya</s>.
	'<s>Aṭavī</s>, <s>araṇya</s>, <s>vipina</s>, <s>gahana</s>, <s>kānana</s>, <s>vana</s>' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	Just as in a forest there is the arising of all wild [beings] — animals, birds, trees, shrubs, grains, and the like —
	so too, where there exists the reality of all the constituent parts of <s>dharma</s> such as purity (<s>śauca</s>), bathing (<s>snāna</s>), and so forth — hence <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> means 'the forest of <s>dharma</s>.'
	'A dwelling useful for Buddhists — for Buddhists, a <s>vihāra</s> is feminine' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	Within such a <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s> — 'within' means 'in the middle.'
	And at <s>Vitastātra</s> city — this is the region previously described as <s>Vitastātra</s>. In this very city of <s>Vitastātra</s>, the <s>vihāra</s> named <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> was established by King <s>Aśoka</s>. Thus, upon the establishment of the <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s> and the city of <s>Vitastātra</s> that served as its base, 'what was built as a <s>caitya</s>' — that is, a temple (<s>devatāyatana</s>) was built by that very King <s>Aśoka</s>.
	'<s>Caitya</s>' and '<s>āyatana</s>' are synonymous; a horse-stable is '<s>mandura</s>' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa]. Such was this <s>caitya</s>, whose height the eyes of onlookers were unable to reach.
	Even with effort they could not — and likewise <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s>'s account states that within the <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s> at <s>Vitastātra</s> city,
	'the <s>caitya</s> that was built, whose height was beyond the capacity of eyes to reach' — by this statement:
	At <s>Vitastātra</s> city, having established the Buddhist dwelling named <s>Dharmāraṇya Vihāra</s>, that king built within that very <s>vihāra</s> one such extremely tall <s>caitya</s>.
	The eyes of people wishing to see the top of that <s>caitya</s> were not sufficient to behold its height.
	Due to its extreme height, that <s>caitya</s> was beyond the range of sight — this is the meaning.
	However, in modern times, even the name of this extremely ancient construction is not found anywhere.
	For in this <s>Vitastātra</s> city, not even the slightest trace or mark of the previous construction is visible.
	Some, by mistake, have written the name of this <s>Vitastātra</s> region as '<s>Vatarahel</s>' in their books, and others have written it as '<s>Vithanār</s>.'
	In both those regions, even upon close examination, neither the name nor any sign of a <s>vihāra</s>, <s>caitya</s>, or the like is seen or heard.
	Therefore, the attribution of the name '<s>Vithavatur</s>' to the <s>Vitastātra</s> region is not inconsistent.
	Rather, it is fitting in its meaningfulness, for one should understand that the absence of signs of the <s>vihāra</s> named <s>Dharmāraṇya</s>, the <s>caitya</s> situated therein, and the like, is due to the power of the vast amount of time that has passed.
32. <s>Śrīnagarī</s>

children.translated_text:
Verse 104, number 32: In the reign of this very <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Śrīnagarī</s>.
	First, the etymology of the word <s>Śrīnagarī</s>:
	Those that do not go anywhere — they are '<s>naga</s>' (mountains). That which bestows great splendor through mountains (<s>naga</s>)
	is '<s>nagara</s>' (city). A small <s>nagara</s> is <s>nagarī</s>, just as a small pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>) is <s>ghaṭī</s>.
	'<s>Pūḥ</s>' is feminine; '<s>purī</s>' and '<s>nagarī</s>' are synonyms; '<s>pattana</s>' and '<s>puṭabhedana</s>' [as well] — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	The word '<s>nagarī</s>' also denotes a city; and that <s>nagarī</s> which possesses <s>śrī</s> (splendor) is <s>Śrīnagarī</s>.
	Such a city named <s>Śrīnagarī</s> was built by King <s>Aśoka</s> — this is the meaning.
	Endowed with rising brilliance through wealth (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), beauty (<s>śobhā</s>), and abundant resources, and containing houses built by skilled artisans, possessing the greatness of merit, numbering ninety-six <s>lakṣa</s> (9,600,000) houses — full of and resplendent with such houses was the city he built — this is the meaning.
	And here, <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s> has written:
He, the prosperous one, with ninety-six thousand residences, resplendent with the signs of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity),

children.text: garīyasīṃ purī śrīmāṃś cakre śrīnagarīṃ tṛpa ||
children.translated_text: made the most magnificent city, <s>Śrīnagarī</s> — [thus says] <s>Tṛpa</s>.

children.text:
ityādi |
	ata evāsya rājño 'tisaṃkhyāyutanagaranirmāṇakartṛtvaṃ kavyuktyājñāyate |
	asya śrīnagarīti khyātanagarasyādhunike kāle grāmīṇair nāgarikaiś ca khyāpitaṃ |
	tathā sarvānyadeśaviditaṃ śrīnagar iti prasiddhataraṃ nāma sarvathā vartate |
	asya śrīnagar iti nagarasya niyamitaḥ ko 'pi pradeśo na labhyate |

	asyaivāśokanirmitasya nagarasya nāmnaiva sarvam apīdaṃ maṇḍalaṃ prakhyātaṃ sampannam |
	ata evāsya kaśmīradeśasya sarvāsu dikṣu prathitatām āptaṃ sarvādigdeśanivāsijanaiḥ kathyamānaṃ śrīnagar iti nāma sphuṭatayā vartate |
	kāśmīrakair vinā sarve 'muṃ maṇḍalam anenaiva śrīnagar nāmnākārayanti ca ye kecana pārisekānuvādakartāras tanmatānu-yāyinaś ca te svapustakeṣu |
	asya śrīnagaryākhyasya deśasyāśrayībhūtau dakṣiṇapārśvavāmapārśvau yāv ādhunike kāle dacchunporpargaṇa tathā khourporpargaṇa ityākhyau puragaṇau vartate tāv evāśrayībhūtau bhavata ityādi likhanti arthāt |
	yāv etau dvau puragaṇau stas tayor eva śrīnagarīti nāmāsti |
	atha vāgatasyātikālasya balavatayā tasya śrīnagaryākhyadeśasya cihnabhūtāv iva puragaṇau bhavata iti teṣām abhiprāyaḥ |
	paraṃ tu kalhaṇa-paṇḍitaḥ svapustake dakṣiṇapārśvavāmapārśvāv eva śrīnagarīty ākhyāv ityādi kiṃcid api na likhati |
	atas tat pārisekānuvādināṃ svakapolakalpanaiveti bhadram ||
children.translated_text:
And so forth.
	From this, through poetic expression, it is known that this king was the creator of innumerable cities.
	The name of this well-known city called <s>Śrīnagarī</s>, in modern times, has been declared by both villagers and city-dwellers,
	and the most famous name, known to all other countries, is certainly <s>Śrīnagar</s>.
	No specific delimited region can be found for this city called <s>Śrīnagar</s>.
	From this it is understood that there is no city distinct from this district called <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
	This entire district has become famous by the very name of this city built by <s>Aśoka</s>.
	Therefore, the name <s>Śrīnagar</s>, having attained fame in all directions of the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, spoken by the inhabitants of all regions and directions, clearly exists.
	Except for the Kashmiris themselves, everyone refers to this district by the very name <s>Śrīnagar</s>, and certain Persian translators and their followers, in their books,
	write that the two <s>pargaṇas</s> known in modern times as <s>Dacchunporpargaṇa</s> and <s>Khourporpargaṇa</s>, being the southern and northern sides of this region called <s>Śrīnagarī</s>, are its supporting areas — that is the meaning.
	These two <s>pargaṇas</s> that exist — theirs alone is the name <s>Śrīnagarī</s>.
	Or alternatively, their view is that due to the force of exceedingly ancient time, these two <s>pargaṇas</s> remain as if markers of the region called <s>Śrīnagarī</s>.
	However, <s>Paṇḍita Kalhaṇa</s> does not write anything whatsoever in his book about the southern and northern sides alone being called <s>Śrīnagarī</s>.
	Therefore, that is merely the fabrication of the Persian translators — and so be it.
33. The Stone Rampart (<s>Aśmamaya Prākāra</s>)

children.text:
ślokasaṃ 105 namba 33 asyāśokasya rājye aśmamayaḥ prākāraḥ |
	asya niruktiḥ |
	aśmānaḥ prācuryeṇāsmin atha vā aśmānaḥ prakṛtir vāsyety aśmamayaḥ |
	tad atra pracuraṃ sāsya prakṛtir vety arthe mayaṭ pratyayo 'tra |
	aśmamayaḥ yaḥ prākāraḥ sāla ity arthaḥ |
	prākāro varaṇaḥ sāla ity amaraḥ |
	etādṛśaḥ prākāras tena rājñāśokena sampāditaḥ |
	atra pūrvaṃ nambarapadābhidheyo dvādaśasaṃkhyāko vijayeśvarābhidho yo 'yaṃ pradeśo varṇito 'sti tasminn eva vijayeśvare pūrvakālīnai rājabhiḥ sudhamayaḥ prākāro nirmita āsīt |
	taṃ sudhāmayaṃ prākāraṃ nivārya sa rājā navīnam aśmamayaṃ prākāraṃ kārayām āsa |
	tathā ca paṇḍitakalhaṇaḥ
children.translated_text:
Verse 105, number 33: The stone rampart during the reign of this <s>Aśoka</s>.
	Its etymology:
	That which has stones (<s>aśmānas</s>) in abundance, or that whose material nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) is stone — is <s>aśmamaya</s> (made of stone).
	Here the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix is used in the sense of 'abundant in that' or 'having that as its material nature.'
	<s>Aśmamaya</s> means a <s>prākāra</s> (rampart), that is, a wall (<s>sāla</s>).
	'<s>Prākāra</s>, <s>varaṇa</s>, <s>sāla</s>' — thus says the <s>Amarakośa</s>.
	Such a rampart was constructed by King <s>Aśoka</s>.
	Here, at the very place previously described under number twelve, the region called <s>Vijayeśvara</s>, a plaster rampart (<s>sudhāmaya prākāra</s>) had been built by earlier kings.
	Removing that plaster rampart, that king had a new stone rampart constructed.
	And thus <s>Paṇḍita Kalhaṇa</s> [says]:
Having removed the old plaster [rampart] of <s>Śrī Vijayeśa</s>,
a flawless stone rampart was caused to be built by him.

children.text:
iti |
	asya prākārasyādhunike kāle vinaṣṭatayā nāmāpi na labhyate |
	cihnādivārttā dūrata evāstām |
	ato 'sya kathyamāṇaṃ janair etatkālīnaṃ nāmādikaṃ na likhitam astīti jñeyam |
	kiṃ tv atra kasmiṃścit purātane kāle 'trāśmamayaḥ prākāro 'py āsīd ity ata evāsmin pradeśasaṃgrahe 'sya parigaṇanaṃ kṛtam |
	yathādhunike kāle śrīraṇavīrasiṃhabhūpanirmitaṃ śivasya caityam ādainābhūd iti ||
children.translated_text:
Thus.
	Since this rampart has been destroyed in modern times, not even its name can be found.
	Talk of traces and the like is quite far off.
	Therefore, it should be understood that the contemporary name and other details spoken by people have not been recorded.
	However, since at some ancient time there indeed existed a stone rampart here, it is for this very reason that it has been enumerated in this <s>Pradeśasaṃgraha</s> (Collection of Places).
	Just as in modern times, the temple of <s>Śiva</s> built by King <s>Śrī Raṇavīrasiṃha</s> came into being at that very place.
34. <s>Aśoka Īśvara</s> Temple (<s>Prāsāda</s>)

children.text:

	anayor niruktiḥ |
	avidyamānaḥ śoko manyur yasya so 'śokaḥ |
	manyuśokau tu śuk striyām ity amaraḥ |
	īśanaśīlaḥ īśanadharmā īśanaṃ sādhu karoti yaḥ sa īśvaraḥ |
	etādṛśāv aśokeśvarasaṃjñakau yau prāsādau devatāyatane iti yāvat |
	harmyādi dhanināṃ vāsaḥ prāsādo devabhūbhujām ity amaraḥ |

	yatas tasmin kāle ye kecana tam īśvarābhidhaṃ prāsādaṃ paśyanti sma te tatkṣaṇād eva tasya manohāritvaguṇasampadāṃ camatkāreṇa śokarahitā babhūvur |
	atas tasyāśoketi nāmānvarthatayā pratīyamānaṃ bhāti |
	tathā ca kartum akartum anyathā-kartuṃ sāmarthyaśālina īśvarasyaiva nāmnāpy ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ prāsādaḥ prakhyātiṃ yataḥ prāptavān ato 'yam api sārthakatām eva prāpto bhāti |
	etayor ubhayoḥ prāsādayor aticirantanakālikatayā nirmāṇasya cihnādikam api kiṃcid yato na bhavaty ataḥ kaśmīrabhāṣāyāṃ janair ādhunike kāle kathyamānaṃ kim api nāmādikam atra na likhitaṃ |
	paraṃ tu paṇḍitakalhaṇo yat
children.translated_text:
Verse 106, number 34: In the reign of <s>Aśoka</s>, the two temples (<s>prāsāda</s>) named <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>.
	The etymology of these two:
	He in whom there is no sorrow (<s>śoka</s>) or anger (<s>manyu</s>) is '<s>Aśoka</s>' (sorrowless).
	'<s>Manyu</s>' and '<s>śoka</s>' are [synonymous with] '<s>śuk</s>' (grief), which is feminine — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	He whose nature is to rule (<s>īśana</s>), whose essence is sovereignty, who exercises dominion well — he is '<s>Īśvara</s>' (the Lord).
	Such were the two temples (<s>prāsāda</s>) named <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> — that is, shrines of the deity.
	'Mansions and such are dwellings of the wealthy; a <s>prāsāda</s> (palace/temple) belongs to gods and kings' — thus says <s>Amara</s> [Kośa].
	By this very King <s>Aśoka</s>, previously described, having constructed a stone enclosure wall at the renowned region of <s>Vijayeśvara</s> in this territory, two temples bearing the described pair of names were built in its very assembly-hall.
	For at that time, whoever beheld that temple named <s>Īśvara</s>, at that very moment became free of sorrow through the wonder of its captivating qualities and splendors.
	Therefore, the name '<s>Aśoka</s>' (sorrowless) shines as befitting its meaning.
	And since this second temple gained fame by the very name of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), who possesses the power to do, to undo, and to do otherwise, therefore this [name] too shines as having achieved meaningfulness.
	Since no trace or sign of the construction of both these temples exists due to their extreme antiquity, no name or other detail spoken by people in the Kashmiri language in modern times has been recorded here.
	However, <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Kalhaṇa</s> [writes] that:
In the assembly-hall of <s>Vijayeśa</s> and nearby, he caused to be built,
the peaceful and humble [king] — two temples (<s>prāsāda</s>) named <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.translated_text:
